message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for me to delete my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch. Let me start by going through the situation step by step. First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom were on a trip. I brought my Switch because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute. My stepbrother really liked playing on it, so I made a new profile for him so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That worked well because it helped distract him while I studied. When I got back to school, I got annoyed because every time I started a game or went to the eShop, I had to click on my profile. So, I decided to delete his profile. Now, during Thanksgiving, my stepbrother found out his Zelda save was gone and started crying, which made me feel bad. My dad thinks it was mean of me because he knew my stepbrother was enjoying playing. I need to consider a few things here. First, was it my right to delete the profile? The Switch is mine, so technically, I can do whatever I want with it. But my stepbrother was using it with my permission, and I created the profile for him. So, by deleting it, I took away something I had given him. Another point is the emotional impact. My stepbrother was upset, and that's a valid reaction. Losing something you were enjoying, especially a game save, can be really frustrating. My dad's perspective is important too; he thinks it was mean, which suggests that from his point of view, it wasn't the kindest thing to do. I also need to think about the bigger picture. Family relationships are important, and actions that hurt others, even if they seem minor, can affect those relationships. Deleting the profile might have been a small inconvenience for me, but it was a big deal for my stepbrother. On the other hand, I was annoyed by having to switch profiles every time. That's a valid feeling too. But maybe there was a better way to handle it, like explaining to my stepbrother why I needed to delete his profile or finding another solution together. In the end, while I had the right to manage my Switch, the way I handled it caused hurt feelings. It might have been better to communicate my needs and find a compromise instead of deleting the profile without discussing it first.
